brand.audience: People seeking domestic cleaning for their own homes across the UK.
facts: We are the premier provider of domestic & home cleaning throughout the UK.
Our domestic cleaning service provides a fully vetted, reference checked and insured cleaner to your home that will deliver a professional clean to suit your individual needs.
We first carry out a telephone interview.
If the applicant seems suitable, we then arrange for a more thorough interview to take place in their own home.
Only after taking proof of ID and address along with references do we accept them onto our database.
We then monitor every cleaner thoroughly for the whole time they are with us.
Once we choose a cleaner for you, we'll arrange for them to come along and meet you so that you can approve our choice and discuss the cleaning tasks you require.
It's important that your cleaner is someone you like so there's no need to agree to the first person we send you.
Once you're satisfied that we've sent the right person for you, you can then mutually arrange a regular clean day and time.
If you'd like to skip the interview and go straight to cleaning this can also be arranged.
Yes. Cleaners use the supplies and equipment already in the home.
We ask that bleach is not used, for health and safety reasons.

brand.offer: A UK domestic cleaning agency that sources vetted, reference-checked and insured cleaners for individual home-cleaning needs.

You don't have to accept the first cleaner introduced.

angles.idea: Meet the cleaner before you decide
angles.usefulInsight: Content job: resolve a meaningful buying hesitation about inviting a cleaner into a private home. Awareness hypothesis: readers know they want help with cleaning but may assume the agency's first choice is final. Opening/payoff pair: ask whether they can meet the cleaner first, then explain the checks, the optional meeting, the right to decline the first person and how the regular arrangement follows approval. Supported mechanism: Maid2Clean's documented vetting and introduction process. Framework: objection → answer → demonstration. Five-slide story: 1) the meeting question and direct answer; 2) what vetting involves, shown as a short ordered diagram; 3) what the meeting is for—approval and discussion of tasks; 4) the useful distinction that the first introduction is not an obligation to accept; 5) once satisfied, mutually arrange the regular day and time, with one FAQ action. Reader payoff: distinguish agency checks from their own decision about personal fit. Image relationship: image-1 or image-2 can establish the private-home setting on the cover, without implying the visible person is a cleaner or customer. Subsequent slides should make the actual process the focal point.

evidence: Do I need to provide cleaning supplies and equipment?
Yes. Cleaners use the supplies and equipment already in the home.
Most clients prefer to choose what is used.
We ask that bleach is not used, for health and safety reasons.
hooks: Your house cleaner uses your supplies and equipment.
Before the first clean: keep your cleaning kit ready.
angles.idea: Your cleaner uses the supplies already in your home
angles.usefulInsight: Content job: make first-clean preparation tangible through a service detail buyers may not expect. Awareness hypothesis: some readers assume a domestic cleaner brings a standard kit. Opening/payoff pair: ask who supplies the cleaning products, then answer clearly that Maid2Clean cleaners use the home's existing supplies and equipment and that bleach should not be used. Supported mechanism: the documented equipment and supplies policy. Framework: question → practical difference → reader preparation. One-frame story: a Maid2Clean-authored ruled note headed 'Who supplies the cleaning products?' with a concise answer covering supplies, equipment and the no-bleach instruction. This is a complete standalone service explanation, not a teaser for the carousel. Reader payoff: know what must already be available at home and one explicit restriction. Image relationship: type-only is appropriate because none of the supplied photographs shows cleaning supplies or equipment; unrelated portraits or phone imagery would weaken the explanation.

evidence: It depends on the size of your home, how many rooms and how much is in them, plus the quality and depth of cleaning that you require.
Ultimately the choice is yours, and you may want fewer or more hours and then prioritise the rooms and jobs to be completed.
Rates vary depending on the area you're in and the number of hours you require each week.
All we require from you is the approximate number of hours you need and your postcode.
hooks: How many cleaning hours does your home need?
Room count isn't the whole cleaning-hours question.
Before choosing cleaning hours, choose your priorities.
angles.idea: Choose cleaning hours around the work, not just the room count
angles.usefulInsight: Content job: help a buyer frame a useful cleaning enquiry without inventing a universal hours estimate. Awareness hypothesis: readers may expect one fixed number of hours for a home of a given size. Opening/payoff pair: ask how many hours to book, then explain that room contents and cleaning depth also matter and that buyers can prioritise rooms and jobs. Supported mechanism: the FAQ describes the factors affecting hours and asks for approximate hours plus postcode when requesting a quote. Framework: belief → distinction → practical example → action. A potential carousel would progress from room count to contents, depth and priorities before explaining the information required for a quote. Any worked example would be explicitly hypothetical and would not assign unsupported cleaning times. Reader payoff: understand what to consider before estimating hours. Image relationship: image-2 could show a furnished domestic setting, but it cannot demonstrate a required duration or cleaning standard.

A patterned throw introduces muted red, black and beige; the composition is wide, airy and predominantly white. image-2 shows a tighter, taller view of the same bedroom setting: the bed and patterned throw fill the left foreground, wooden floorboards lead toward the black-framed doorway, and a partly cropped person stands near the bright opening. image-3 shows a person from behind with shoulder-length light hair and a pale top, facing a small visible screen. The softly lit interior includes pale seating, a plant on the right and a muted green cast; the person occupies the left side. image-4 shows a smiling person with shoulder-length dark hair wearing a navy T-shirt, positioned on the right against a pale pink-grey background, with a light curved surface across the lower foreground and generous empty space on the left. image-6 is a close-up of hands holding and touching a smartphone; a white shirt fills the right foreground and deep blue upholstery forms much of the background. Screen details are not legible enough to describe a workflow. None of these images establishes a person's identity, customer status or cleaning outcome. Instagram and LinkedIn can address the same household buyer; no founder framing is warranted. Use one FAQ next action per post. posts.altText: Five-slide Maid2Clean carousel in peach, black and white. The cover pairs a bright bedroom setting with a question about meeting a cleaner first; the photograph illustrates a home, not a cleaning result. The next slides explain telephone and home interviews, identity and reference checks, the opportunity to meet and discuss tasks, the right not to accept the first person, and arranging a regular day and time once satisfied.
posts.caption:
Choosing someone to clean your home involves more than agreeing a time. Maid2Clean's checks and your chance to discuss the tasks serve different purposes: the agency vets the cleaner, while the introduction lets you decide whether you're comfortable with the choice.

The meeting is optional. If you'd prefer to skip it and go straight to cleaning, that can also be arranged.

Read the service FAQs before enquiring: maid2clean.co.uk/faqs/

h3: How can we help?
p: If you don't find the question you're looking for, don't worry, just get in touch with us and we'll help you the best we can.
h3: How many hours do I need?
p: It depends on the size of your home, how many rooms and how much is in them, plus the quality and depth of cleaning that you require.
p: Ultimately the choice is yours, and you may want fewer or more hours and then prioritise the rooms and jobs to be completed.
p: Below is a general guide for various property sizes:
h3: How much will I pay?
p: Our hourly rates include the cleaner's wage and the agency fee. Rates vary depending on the area you're in and the number of hours you require each week. If you'd like a free quote, then contact us! All we require from you is the approximate number of hours you need and your postcode.
h3: What time is your office open until?
p: The majority of our offices are open late and available at least 6 days of the week. Go to your local office to find out the opening times.
h3: What sort of contract am I tied in to?
p: We don't believe in long and complicated contracts and do believe in being fair. Naturally, like any business, we have to have terms and conditions, and these can be found in the footer of any page. If you do ever need to cancel, all we ask is that you give us two month's notice or notice in accordance with the billing letter provided from your local office.
h3: How do you vet the cleaners?
p: We first carry out a telephone interview. If the applicant seems suitable, we then arrange for a more thorough interview to take place in their own home. Only after taking proof of ID and address along with references do we accept them onto our database. We then monitor every cleaner thoroughly for the whole time they are with us.
h3: Do I meet my cleaner before the first clean?
p: Of course! We know the cleaner will be in your home and that personalities are often as important as cleaning standards. Once we choose a cleaner for you, we'll arrange for them to come along and meet you so that you can approve our choice and discuss the cleaning tasks you require. It's important that your cleaner is someone you like so there's no need to agree to the first person we send you. Once you're satisfied that we've sent the right person for you, you can then mutually arrange a regular clean day and time. If you'd like to skip the interview and go straight to cleaning this can also be arranged.
h3: What if my cleaner can't make it, or is sick?
p: Just give us a call, and we will provide you with a cleaner to cover.
h3: Can I have an evening or weekend clean?
p: Yes of course! Our cleaners are fully flexible and will take on evening or weekend cleaning work. Please note in certain areas a supplement hourly charge may be added for cleans after 6pm or at weekends.
h3: Can I have a clean once a month?
p: Most of our offices do not do monthly cleans - typically our most infrequent clean is every fortnight, or a one off.
h3: Will I have to be at home when my cleaner visits?
p: No, our cleaners are vetted and are happy to hold your house keys. We will provide you with a Key Acknowledgement Form for your cleaner to sign.
h3: Do I need to provide cleaning supplies and equipment?
p: Yes. Cleaners use the supplies and equipment already in the home. Most clients prefer to choose what is used. We ask that bleach is not used, for health and safety reasons.
h3: Can I change my cleaner if I am not happy?
p: Yes, of course, we have a large and varied cleaner base, and we'd be happy to assign you someone different if you are unhappy for any reason. Just give us a call.
h3: Do you have insurance cover?
p: Yes. Public liability insurance of at least £1,000,000 is in place, subject to our terms of business. The policy is indemnity cover, not new for old. Claims remain subject to liability being established and to the terms, conditions, exclusions and excesses of the policy. There is a £100 excess per claim. Where appropriate, customers should approach their household insurer first, as set out in our terms of business.
